6106.overview:
Otogi: Myth of Demons is a third-person action game which lets you play as Raikoh. Once a mighty warrior, he has been resurrected by a mysterious princess to free Japan of an army of demons and is held in the world of the living by her powers.

Battle your enemies with either your sword, your magic, or both, and buy new weapons, spells and other items between missions to better your performance. The battle system, while simple at its roots, lets you execute a number of combinations of basic, heavy, spell, and dash attacks to strike at your enemies. Since Raikoh can stay long in mid-air and even rise up higher by executing certain slashes, fights take place in all three directions of the area.

6107.overview:
Otogi 2: Immortal Warriors combines fantasy with real life folklore and fast paced action. It starts where its predecessor ended and this time Raikoh, the hero of the first game, is not alone. Five new warriors join him and combine their powers to tackle the task of saving the world from a new demonic threat.

Gameplay is pretty much your regular hack & slash, and there is lots of it. The player advances through levels, destroying huge amounts of mystical enemies with different attacks, both physical and magical, while collecting experience which lets one improve the skills of the characters. New weapons and accessories can be purchased from a store between levels. Challenge levels separate from the main game open up as levels are completed, such as ones that task you wish surviving against a never ending horde of monsters, or destroying 100 arches in a limited time. Almost everything in the game's levels are destroyable, from trees to buildings, and the six playable characters are all different so one level might be easier to complete with one character than the other.

6108.overview: A Blockbuster Video Exclusive release. This is another 9 holiday holes of Outlaw Golf like last year's Outlaw Golf: Holiday Golf. This time it's Summer and Trey in their holiday dress playing on 9 never-before seen courses. This short version has all the clubs unlocked, so use that bigger stick.

6109.overview:
Outlaw Volleyball is the second game in Simon & Schuster's growing Outlaw franchise.

As the title suggests, you play various games of volleyball with shady and dirty characters, from a slutty biker to an ex con to a pair of strippers. There are sixteen players in total. Each character has his or her own unique personality, strengths and weaknesses.

There are four different modes you can compete in; Exhibition, which is a standard volleyball game, Tour, which is the career mode that spans fifty different events, and Drills, which are sort of like practice games that awards points you can use to improve your player's abilities. The fourth mode is Xbox Live enabled, allowing you to play with people over the Xbox Live service.

There are ten different courts to play on, each one with it's own backgrounds and animation. You can play on a beach, at a carnival, or even in a prison.

Outlaw Volleyball utilizes the same momentum feature first seen in Outlaw Golf, which allows you to earn "beating tokens" that you can spend on beating up the other team. If you are doing lousy, beating up a member of the other team refills your momentum meter, allowing you to come back and possibly win.

6110.overview: Arcade style racing action meets challenge based skills driving. Driving between different zones to reach the finish point with choices of which route to take along the way means you can select the difficulty along the way. This is the sequel to the original arcade classic and has a very similar style graphically and gameplay.

8030.overview:
Something is very wrong at Leafmore High. The entire school has turned dark and foreboding, strange sounds echo in the halls, and several people have mysteriously gone missing. One group of brave teens decides to find out what's going on... no matter what. They have no idea what kind of horrors have gripped the school and everyone in it. In the darkness, the evil has power... but add light and they can be defeated. Will they survive the night ahead?

In Solo Mode, choose from 5 characters with different personalities, aptitude and perspectives. Change between them at any time (as long as they are still alive).

The player can also select a second person (as a "teammate") to accompany the player by going to a "gathering point" in the game. At any time during play, the player can switch control between the first character and the second, thereby accessing their special talents.

There are several basic types of weapons used in the game: contact (a baseball bat for instance), pistols, guns, and more exotic, high-powered "special" weapons. Ammunition is specific for each gun or pistol and is not interchangeable. Weapons can be swapped between characters and ammunition found is stored in the group's reserves for sharing amongst them.

8031.overview: In Oddworld Stranger's Wrath, the new chapter the Oddworld series, you'll step into the role of the Stranger--a mysterious bounty hunter who tracks down outlaws for money. Equipped a variety of strange weapons that use small creatures as bullets, you'll explore expansive environments ranging from Old West towns and thick forests to industrial complexes. The game combines first- and third-person action gameplay with familiar Oddworld elements.

10395.overview: In Oddworld, you played as a former slave/worker that, almost despite himself, rose to lead his Mudokon people against the evil corporate scumbags the Glukkons. In Munch you're introduced to a new race, the Gabbits, who have been driven to extinction simply because their lungs happen to match the chain-smoking Glukkon's size and fit for replacement surgery. To make matters worse, Munch has been implanted with a sonic device by the Vykkers in an experiment, and is to be used to capture more creatures. With the help of the Fuzzles, big-toothed fuzzballs used for product testing, Munch escapes, meets up with Abe, and together they set out to stop the Glukkons at their game... not to mention win back the last can of Gabbiar -- Gabbit eggs -- in the world.

10590.overview: OutRun 2006: Coast 2 Coast features 15 unique cars, the most ever seen in any OutRun game. In addition to the ten cars from OutRun 2 SP, new models include the 550 Barchetta, F355 Spider, Superamerica, 328 GTS, and the Ferrari F430. Some models cannot be unlocked on the PlayStation Portable or PlayStation 2 without the use of the cross-system connectivity feature inherent of the two systems.

15036.overview: Golf meets strippers, ex-cons, and wannabe rappers. In Outlaw Golf, you can step into the shoes of all kinds of criminals and compete in 30 tour events. With each event, you'll unlock new characters and better equipment and improve your character's skills. Challenge three of your friends in eight different games, including stroke, match, skins, best ball, casino, and more. Play like a pro and the game gets easier; play poorly and the game becomes tougher.

15037.overview: The crude cast of Outlaw Golf is back with new friends, courses, fighting moves, and more. Choose from 11 wild characters--including babes, rappers, and thugs--and take on the challenges from eight courses, ranging from the arctic to the jungle. By playing through the tour and winning events, you can unlock more clubs, balls, and outfits. In addition to tournament mode, the game features match, time attack, and baseball golf modes. Just remember--even if your golf game is off, you can still beat up your opponents, or even your caddy.

17066.overview:
The Outlaw gang is back, this time to take on the world of Tennis. The game features all your favorite characters from the previous Outlaw games and adds a few new ones for a total of 16 playable characters. Like the other Outlaw games, there are a number of unlock-able items including new characters, racquets, balls, courts and mini-games and a hard rock soundtrack.

The game follows the traditional rules of tennis and adds the unique humor and special features common to the series including player fights, exploding balls, changing weather, character improvements, outfits and other accessories.

There are 6 game modes including: Exhibition, Tour (50 Tour Matches - Singles, Doubles & Canadian Doubles mixed), Random Play, Drills and Network play. Special matches include Classic, Hot Potato, Casino, Baseball, Football, Pinball and Ping Pong which are similar in nature to the other games in the series.

95297.overview: A Blockbuster Video Exclusive game for the 2003 Halloween season. This acts like a demo for those not familiar with Outlaw Volleyball and has some new features for those who are. Some of the new items: Halloween costumes for many of the female characters and a new court.

125665.overview:
Over the Hedge is a 2006 video game based on the film of the same name that serves as its direct-to-video-game sequel.

This was the last DreamWorks Animation game released for the Xbox.

Sami Kirkpatrick, Madison Davenport and Shane Baumel reprise their roles from the film as Bucky, Squillo, and Spike.

153790.overview:
Operation Flashpoint: Elite is a port of the original Operation Flashpoint and its expansion Resistance for Xbox, but adds some additional content. It also includes individual single missions, a mission editor and co-op or competitive online play over Xbox Live. 

As with the PC release, Operation Flashpoint: Elite is a realistic soldier simulation where player get to control both individual soldiers, full squads and various vehicles including helicopters and tanks. In total the campaigns contain more than 60 missions. Through Xbox Live, 50 multiplayer missions are available.

153791.overview: It's the holidays and here are 9 all-new holes for the holidays. A small taste of Outlaw Golf but on slippery slopes, frozen greens, and other cold wintery conditions to challenge you on these courses.

153794.overview: Open Season is a video game, based on the movie of the same name. It was released for Wii, PlayStation 2, PlayStation Portable, Microsoft Windows, Game Boy Advance, Xbox 360, Xbox, Nintendo DS, and Nintendo GameCube. The Nintendo DS version supports the Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection.

153856.overview: A rogue U.S. Special Forces unit dubbed "Black Hand" has joined forces with a terrorist group called "The Minutemen." Together they have taken control of a vast nuclear arsenal in a top secret military installation at sea and seized the activation codes for a weapon known only as "Project Poseidon." The fate of the world hangs by a thread, and a few ticks of the clock means the difference between justice and annihilation. The player controls one or two of the three CRT (Crisis Response Team) members. Led by CO Jack Walcott, the new WinBack assault team is composed of three young, yet combat-proven, operatives led by Craig Contrell. Each team member is qualified in six different weapon types and highly-adept at close quarters combat (CQC). The player's objective is to complete 30 missions of action, strategy, stealth, rescuing, escorting, and various types of essential goals to stop the terrorists.

456080.overview:
OXM Demo Disc 7 (June 2002)

Playable game demos: Dead or Alive 3 (new demo), Epic Smash Bros., Burnout, Toxic Battle Blast 2, The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, Halo (special demo), Twisted Plastic: Black, Mercy's Meeting: Rise of Star-Lla, Circus Maximus: Chariot Wars, All Star Baseball 2003, Jet Set Radio Future, Max Payne, Test Drive Off-Road: Wide Open, Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX 2

Video previews: Bloodwake, MLB Slugfest 20-03, Outlaw Golf, The Wild Chaos: World Animal Rally!, Toxic Grind, Woody Woodpecker: Escape from Buzz Buzzard's Park

includes exclusive DOA Booster expansion for DOA3.

479711.overview: OpenJKDF2x is an original Xbox port of OpenJKDF2.

481054.overview:
The disc included with Official Xbox Magazine Volume 01, December 2001, was the first OXM demo disc for the original Xbox. It showcased the console’s launch lineup through playable game demos, trailers, preview videos, and promotional material about Xbox games and accessories.

It was not a full retail game or system-update disc; its purpose was to let new Xbox owners sample launch-era titles and learn more about the console’s software and features.

481055.overview: The demo disc included with Official Xbox Magazine – Issue #2 (January 2002) features five playable titles spanning diverse genres: Oddworld: Munch’s Oddysee, Cel Damage, Fuzion Frenzy, 4x4 EVO 2, and Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2x. Alongside these interactive demos, the compilation includes video trailers for upcoming Xbox blockbusters such as Halo: Combat Evolved, Jet Set Radio Future, Amped: Freestyle Snowboarding, Blood Wake, Mad Dash Racing, NightCaster, and Sega GT 2002.

481083.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #05 was released alongside Issue 5 of the magazine in March 2002 (carrying the cover date of April 2002). Serving as another early showcase for the original Xbox console library, the disc featured four full interactive playable game demos: snowboarding title Amped: Freestyle Snowboarding, extreme sports title Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX 2, fighting game Dead or Alive 3, and high-speed driving action game Wreckless: The Yakuza Missions.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc included non-playable video previews for upcoming titles such as RalliSport Challenge, NBA Inside Drive 2002, and Gunvalkyrie. It also contained video featurettes, including a special appearance by UFC fighter Chuck Liddell, an exclusive first look at Malice, and the magazine's Top 10 Plays of the Month.

481084.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #06 was released alongside Issue 6 of the magazine in April 2002 (bearing the cover date of May 2002). The disc offered a robust selection of five full interactive game demos: Sega's fast-paced third-person shooter GunValkyrie, high-octane rally racer RalliSport Challenge, snowboarding adventure Dark Summit, Microsoft's first-party sports sim NBA Inside Drive 2002, and the platforming adventure Oddworld: Munch's Oddysee.

Beyond the interactive playable roster, the disc contained non-playable video features, walkthroughs, and trailers. Highlights included behind-the-scenes footage for Titus's Superman, a video walkthrough for Wreckless: The Yakuza Missions, a segment showcasing a "Perfect Run" in Project Gotham Racing, and OXM's Top 10 Plays of the Month.

481085.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #08 was released alongside Issue 8 of the magazine in June 2002 (bearing the cover date of July 2002). The disc showcased prominent summer Xbox titles with five playable game demos: action tie-in Spider-Man: The Movie, platformer Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex, high-speed motorcycle simulator MotoGP: Ultimate Racing Technology, sci-fi flight combat game Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter, and EA's baseball sim Triple Play 2002.

Beyond the main playable roster, the disc featured downloadable content in the form of a Dead or Alive 3 Bonus Pack (costumes/content). It also included various developer segments and media features, such as a behind-the-scenes motion-capture session for Bike: Street, Dirt, Vert, a strategy guide video for Blood Omen 2, developer commentary with Bungie, a preview of Crazy Taxi 3: High Roller, a "Making of NFL Blitz" featurette, and OXM's Top 10 Plays of the Month.

481086.overview: The Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #03 was released alongside Issue 3 of the magazine in January 2002 (bearing the cover/issue date of February 2002). Designed to showcase the early library of the original Xbox following its North American launch, this disc contained six playable game demos along with video features highlighting upcoming software.   The playable roster offered a mix of genres, including action-adventure title Azurik: Rise of Perathia, high-speed flight combat game AirForce Delta Storm, chaotic obstacle-course racer Mad Dash Racing, stock-car simulator NASCAR Thunder 2002, and sports titles NFL Fever 2002 and NHL Hitz 20-02. Alongside the games, the disc featured non-playable content such as behind-the-scenes footage from the "Making of NASCAR Thunder 2002," early looks at titles like Circus Maximus: Chariot Wars and Wreckless: The Yakuza Missions, and coverage of OXM's presence in Tokyo.

481090.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #09 was released alongside Issue 9 of the magazine in July 2002 (bearing the cover date of August 2002). This issue focused on prominent mid-2002 releases, featuring five full playable game demos: arcade-style open-world racer Crazy Taxi 3: High Roller, action-adventure title Enclave, third-person action game Bruce Lee: Quest for the Dragon, futuristic hovercraft racer TD Overdrive: The Brotherhood of Speed (released in North America as Test Drive), and baseball simulator World Series Baseball.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc included non-playable media and video features. Highlights included video walkthroughs and strategy guides for Dead or Alive 3 (demonstrating how to unlock costumes), previews and gameplay trailers for upcoming titles like Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Outlaw Golf, and The Thing, as well as OXM’s monthly reader replay segments and Top Plays.

481091.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #04 was released alongside Issue 4 of the magazine in February 2002 (carrying the cover date of March 2002). Continuing to highlight the early lineup for the original Xbox, this disc featured three main playable demos—the arcade combat racer Arctic Thunder, the vehicular naval combat game Blood Wake, and the flagship racing simulator Project Gotham Racing—along with a "Bonus Demo Pack" re-offering selectable demos from previous OXM discs.

In addition to playable games, the disc contained non-playable media and video features, including "The Making of The Thing" trailer, video previews for Hunter: The Reckoning and Yager, footage highlighting Halo: Combat Evolved's legendary ending, and promotional segments like "Xbox Unleashed" and Top Plays of the Month.

481099.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #10 was released alongside Issue 10 of the magazine in August 2002 (bearing the cover date of September 2002). Highlighting a prominent selection of late-summer releases, the disc featured four full interactive playable game demos: comic sports game Outlaw Golf, supernatural action-adventure title Buffy the Vampire Slayer, futuristic hovercraft racer Quantum Redshift, and extreme inline-skating game Aggressive Inline.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc provided downloadable content (DLC) saves and extra media features. Highlights included bonus costume content for Dead or Alive 3, strategy videos, and video previews for upcoming titles like Turok: Evolution, Unreal Championship, and Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance, alongside OXM's monthly Top Plays segment.

481101.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #11 was released alongside Issue 11 of the magazine in September 2002 (bearing the cover date of October 2002). The disc featured a flagship interactive demo for the highly anticipated sci-fi shooter TimeSplitters 2, alongside a curated "Best of Playable Demos" sampler collection from previous OXM releases. The interactive lineup included Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex, Halo: Combat Evolved, Hunter: The Reckoning, Max Payne, Spider-Man: The Movie, and Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter.

In addition to interactive gameplay, the disc included non-playable video previews for upcoming blockbusters, including early looks at Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, ToeJam & Earl III: Mission to Earth, and Lotus Challenge. It also featured video segments such as a featurette on the band No Doubt in relation to Malice, game walkthroughs, and OXM's monthly Top Plays.

481104.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #12 was released alongside Issue 12 of the magazine in October 2002 (bearing the cover date of November 2002). This disc celebrated the 1-year anniversary of the Xbox console and featured five full interactive playable game demos: survival horror action game The Thing, vehicular combat title Taz: Wanted, extreme sports sim Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4, fast-paced racing game Sega GT 2002, and open-world action title Hitman 2: Silent Assassin.

Alongside playable demos, the disc contained video features and previews for major holiday blockbusters, including early looks at Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, Blinx: The Time Sweeper, and Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball. It also included DLC saves and featurette videos like OXM's monthly Top Plays.

481108.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #13 was released alongside Issue 13 of the magazine in November 2002 (bearing the cover date of Holiday 2002 or December 2002). Marking the first anniversary of the Xbox, this disc featured six playable game demos highlighting the 2002 holiday season: third-person action game ToeJam & Earl III: Mission to Earth, tactical action shooter Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon, sci-fi vehicular combat title RoboTech: Battlecry, arcade off-road racer ATV Quad Power Racing 2, extreme sports game BMX XXX, and SEGA's time-manipulating platformer Blinx: The Time Sweeper.

Beyond playable demos, the disc included video trailers and behind-the-scenes previews for high-profile upcoming titles like Unreal Championship, Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. It also featured downloadable content (DLC) saves and OXM’s regular Top Plays of the Month.

481110.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #14 was released alongside Issue 14 of the magazine in December 2002 (bearing the cover date of January 2003). Serving as a showcase for early 2003 releases and Xbox Live's initial launch push, the disc featured five main interactive playable game demos: action-shooter Dead to Rights, arcade racer Burnout, sci-fi action title Minority Report: Everybody Runs, stealth-action shooter Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, and extreme sports game Kelly Slater's Pro Surfer.

In addition to the main playable demos, the disc contained non-playable video previews and trailers for upcoming Xbox Live titles and games like Steel Battalion, Panzer Dragoon Orta, Brute Force, and MechAssault. It also included DLC content (such as new maps and game saves) and OXM's monthly Top Plays of the Month.

481111.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #17 was released alongside Issue 17 of the magazine in March 2003 (bearing the cover date of April 2003). The disc featured three main interactive playable game demos: Microsoft's comedic party brawler Kung Fu Chaos, high-speed racing title Apex, and Acclaim's sports sim All-Star Baseball 2004. It also featured a "Select Demos" section re-offering previously highlighted hits such as Halo: Combat Evolved, Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, Panzer Dragoon Orta, and TimeSplitters 2.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc contained non-playable video features and trailers for upcoming titles like Evil Dead: A Fistful of Boomstick, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, Jurassic Park: Operation Genesis, Rally Fusion, Sudeki, and Tao Feng: Fist of the Lotus, along with OXM's regular Top Plays of the Month.

481112.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #20 was released alongside Issue 20 of the magazine in June 2003 (bearing the cover date of July 2003). Highlighting the summer 2003 Xbox lineup and early Xbox Live integration, the disc featured five full interactive playable game demos: squad-based action shooter Brute Force, open-world arcade racer Midtown Madness 3, movie tie-in action title Enter the Matrix, arcade golf game Outlaw Golf: 9 More Holes X-Mas (a special holiday extension course), and motocross title MX Superfly.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc contained non-playable video previews and trailers for upcoming blockbusters, including early looks at Dino Crisis 3, Otogi: Myth of Demons, and Grabbed by the Ghoulies. It also featured downloadable content (DLC) content/saves and OXM's monthly Top Plays segment.

481113.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #23 was released alongside Issue 23 of the magazine in September 2003 (bearing the cover date of October 2003). Setting the stage for the fall 2003 blockbuster season, the disc featured four full interactive playable game demos: Namco’s acclaimed weapon-based 3D fighter Soulcalibur II, fantasy action-RPG Dungeons & Dragons: Heroes, vehicular combat title RoadKill, and football simulation NFL Fever 2004.

Alongside the playable roster, the disc included downloadable content (DLC) saves and extra media features. Highlights featured non-playable video trailers and behind-the-scenes previews for upcoming titles such as True Crime: Streets of LA, Castlevania: Curse of Darkness, and Counter-Strike, along with OXM's monthly Top Plays of the Month.

481114.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #25 was released alongside Issue 25 of the magazine in November 2003 (bearing the cover date of Holiday 2003). Marking the magazine's second anniversary issue, the disc showcased peak 2003 holiday releases with five full interactive playable game demos: acclaimed tactical shooter Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3, flagship racing simulator Project Gotham Racing 2, flight combat game Secret Weapons Over Normandy, action-adventure title Sphinx and the Cursed Mummy, and extreme sports game SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom.

In addition to the playable roster, the disc included Xbox Live downloadable content (DLC) saves and extra media features. Highlights featured non-playable video trailers, strategy walkthroughs, and developer interviews for high-profile upcoming titles like Halo 2, Ninja Gaiden, and Deus Ex: Invisible War, along with OXM's monthly Top Plays segment.

481115.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #26 was released alongside Issue 26 of the magazine in December 2003 (bearing the cover date of January 2004). Highlighting the early 2004 lineup and post-holiday Xbox releases, the disc featured five full interactive playable game demos: immersive sci-fi action-RPG Deus Ex: Invisible War, fast-paced futuristic hover-racer Powerdrome, tactical military shooter Conflict: Desert Storm II – Back to Baghdad, arcade off-road racer ATV Quad Power Racing 2, and arcade skateboarding title Disney's Extreme Skate Adventure.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc provided downloadable content (DLC) saves and extra media features. Highlights featured non-playable video trailers, behind-the-scenes previews, and featurettes for upcoming titles like Ninja Gaiden, Unreal Championship 2, and Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball, along with OXM's regular Top Plays of the Month.

481116.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #15 was released alongside Issue 15 of the magazine in January 2003 (bearing the cover date of February 2003). The disc featured six interactive playable game demos across a range of genres: sci-fi mecha shooter Battle Engine Aquila, SEGA's open-world adventure Shenmue II, movie tie-in action game Reign of Fire, futuristic hover-racer Quantum Redshift, off-road racer ATV Quad Power Racing 2, and snowboarding title TransWorld Snowboarding.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc included downloadable content (DLC) saves and non-playable video features, including trailers and behind-the-scenes previews for upcoming Xbox releases, along with OXM's regular Top Plays of the Month.

481117.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #16 was released alongside Issue 16 of the magazine in February 2003 (bearing the cover date of March 2003). Highlighting early spring 2003 releases, the disc featured five full interactive playable game demos: SEGA's rail-shooter Panzer Dragoon Orta, first-person mech shooter MechAssault, arcade racer Micro Machines, action-platformer Vexx, and EA Sports' skateboarding sim Street Hoops.

Beyond the playable lineup, the disc featured downloadable content (DLC) saves, including bonus content for ToeJam & Earl III: Mission to Earth and Dead or Alive 3. It also included video trailers and previews for upcoming titles such as Brute Force, Midtown Madness 3, and Indiana Jones and the Emperor's Tomb, along with OXM's monthly Top Plays.

481118.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #18 was released alongside Issue 18 of the magazine in April 2003 (bearing the cover date of May 2003). The disc headlined a featured playable demo for the iconic squad-based first-person shooter Return to Castle Wolfenstein: Tides of War.

Alongside the main interactive gameplay, the disc included downloadable content (DLC) saves and extra media features. Highlights featured video trailers and early looks for upcoming titles such as Final Fantasy X-2, True Crime: Streets of LA, Sudeki, and Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, along with game walkthroughs and OXM's monthly Top Plays segment.

481119.overview:

Tao Feng: Fist of the Lotus (3D fighting game)

Colin McRae Rally 3.0 (rally racing)

MotoGP 2 (motorcycle racing)

Pro Race Driver (touring car racing)

481120.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #21 was released alongside Issue 21 of the magazine in July 2003 (bearing the cover date of August 2003). Serving as a showcase for mid-summer 2003 releases, the disc featured four full interactive playable game demos: action-platformer Voodoo Vince, sci-fi shooter Mace Griffin: Bounty Hunter, arcade combat racer Splashdown: Rides Gone Wild, and motorcycle racing simulator MotoGP 2.

Highlights featured non-playable video trailers and first-look previews for upcoming titles such as Dungeons & Dragons: Heroes, Gladius, and Freedom Fighters, alongside OXM's monthly Top Plays segment.

481121.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #22 was released alongside Issue 22 of the magazine in August 2003 (bearing the cover date of September 2003). Highlighting late-summer releases, the disc featured four full interactive playable game demos: SEGA's hack-and-slash action game Otogi: Myth of Demons, action-adventure movie tie-in The Great Escape, tactical action title Freedom Fighters, and college football simulator NCAA Football 2004.

In addition to interactive demos, the disc included non-playable video features and previews for upcoming titles such as Grabbed by the Ghoulies, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Soulcalibur II, and Project Gotham Racing 2. It also contained downloadable content (DLC) saves and OXM's regular Top Plays of the Month.

481122.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #24 was released alongside Issue 24 of the magazine in October 2003 (bearing the cover date of November 2003). Kicking off the peak fall holiday gaming season, the disc featured four full interactive playable game demos: action-platformer Grabbed by the Ghoulies, open-world action-adventure True Crime: Streets of LA, tactical turn-based RPG Gladius, and combat racing game Downtown Run (released in North America as Urban Freestyle Soccer / City Soccer or Super Trick Soccer variations in select regions, or bundled alongside tactical strategy previews).

In addition to interactive demos, the disc featured Xbox Live content, game saves, and non-playable video features. Highlights included trailer previews and strategy segments for upcoming holiday hits like Project Gotham Racing 2, Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3, and Secret Weapons Over Normandy, as well as OXM's monthly Top Plays.

481124.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #27 was released alongside Issue 27 of the magazine in January 2004 (bearing the cover date of February 2004). Highlighting early 2004 titles, the disc featured four full interactive playable game demos: action-adventure reboot Sphinx and the Cursed Mummy, military squad shooter Full Spectrum Warrior, SEGA's arcade racer Sonic Heroes, and sports title NFL Street.

In addition to playable demos, the disc provided downloadable content (DLC) saves and non-playable media features. Highlights included video trailers, strategy guides, and early looks for upcoming hits such as Ninja Gaiden, Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow, and Phantasy Star Online Episode I & II, along with OXM's monthly Top Plays segment.

481126.overview:
Official Xbox Magazine (OXM) Demo Disc #28 was released alongside Issue 28 of the magazine in February 2004 (bearing the cover date of March 2004). Rogue Trooper (tactical third-person sci-fi shooter)
FlatOut 2 (high-speed demolition and arcade racing)
Madden NFL 07 (gridiron football simulation)
NCAA Football 07 (college football simulation)

While the interactive demos ran original Xbox code (playable on Xbox 360 via backward compatibility), the disc dedicated a massive portion of its storage to Xbox 360 HD media and system updates. Highlights included high-definition 720p/1080i video previews for fall 2006 titles like Saints Row, Dead Rising, Gears of War, and Rainbow Six: Vegas, along with downloadable Xbox 360 gamerpics, themes, offline backward-compatibility updates, and OXM's monthly Top Plays segment.
